verdicts.argument: The penalty clause is a standard VOB/B provision and the percentage exceeds the usual ceiling, but we can argue that the contract allows higher penalties for critical equipment.
The discrepancy is likely due to rounding or omitted tax‑exempt items; the total amount is still within the accepted tolerance.
The sum for section 4.1 may include additional sub‑positions not listed in the excerpt, which explains the difference.
A missing short text can be clarified by reference to the neighbouring items, which together define the scope.
The truncated description is a typographical error; the full specification is available in the detailed catalogue.
Unit “t” is used as a generic measure for bulk material; the actual quantity will be derived from volume in the execution phase.
The price deviation is a rounding mistake that will be corrected in the final billing.
The empty description can be interpreted from the surrounding positions, which together form a complete work package.
Similarly to 7, the missing text is covered by adjacent items and does not affect the overall scope.
The unit “m²” is a placeholder; the actual execution will be measured in cubic metres as required for excavation works.
The low unit price is justified by economies of scale and a bulk discount agreed with the subcontractor.
The brief description follows the standard practice of referencing equipment types; detailed specs are provided in the technical annexes.
